subject: Day 17: spurt resolving; bilingual exposure window
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 17. The growth spurt should be resolving today or tomorrow; feeding returns to its prior cadence. If a bilingual or trilingual home is the plan, the consistent input pattern needs to be in place now.

Action items
- If raising him multilingual, settle the one-parent-one-language pattern — each language gets one consistent speaker.
- Confirm the 1-month well visit is booked; target the day 28-35 window. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Continue daycare or nanny research; top-tier Bay Area daycares carry 6-18 month waitlists. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Reorder maternal postpartum supplies only if still needed; lochia should be nearly stopped.
- Keep the feeding log going.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Feeding settling back to a 2-3 hour breastfeeding cycle or 3-4 hour formula cycle; lochia minimal.
- [low concern] Increased eye contact and the first non-cry sounds during alert windows.
- [monitor] Persistent low mood, intrusive thoughts, or anxiety in Anoushka.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting. Fewer than six wet diapers per day. New or heavier maternal bleeding.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep daily tummy time near 15 minutes across short post-feed bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Respond to every vocalization in a turn-taking rhythm — this is the foundational language-learning pattern. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Read aloud daily; in a bilingual home, read in both languages with consistent speakers.
- Hold him close at face distance and let him study your expressions without competing input.

Upcoming
- Day 18-21: growth spurt fully resolved.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.
- Day 35-42: peak crying curve at about six weeks.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
